Engineers have built a small chip-based device that works like a tape measure for light, a development that could improve timekeeping in mobile phones, navigation systems, and data centers. The device uses a tiny ring-shaped waveguide to generate a comb of evenly spaced colors, each of which can be used as a precise reference. Previous versions of the technology required large lab equipment and substantial power; the new chip operates on a few hundred milliwatts and fits on a fingertip. “Our goal is to move this from the laboratory to the field,” said the lead researcher. The team demonstrated that the chip could keep time to within a billionth of a second over a day. The results were published in a peer-reviewed journal, and a commercial partner has expressed interest in licensing the design.
